title: Little Computer People
build: single-file crack by Mr Z (crack screen "CRACKED BY MR Z..."): disk name LCP, one crunched 192-block program COMPUTER PEOPLE; no error bytes

records.c: Jump table the crack copies here from $4B40 before jumping to $0340. $FFFC in RAM also points here: the first entry is the cold start.

The keyboard, as scan_keyboard reads it: 64 ASCII codes indexed by row + 8 * column of the key matrix (row selected through $DC00, column read from $DC01). Special codes: $23 SHIFT, $24 CTRL, $21 a key ignored, $5C no character.
One bit per keyboard column, tested against what $DC01 reads back.
The byte written to $DC00 to select each keyboard row: one bit low.
The game's IRQ handler, reached through $0314 from irq_shim. About three interrupts a frame; $D019 bit 0 separates raster interrupts from the other source, which goes to $8018.
Hardware IRQ entry ($FFFE in RAM; the KERNAL is banked out, $01=$35). Pushes A, X and Y as the KERNAL would and jumps through $0314, so the game keeps a KERNAL-style vector.
Hardware NMI entry ($FFFA in RAM): jumps through $0318, which points at an RTI ($082A), so RESTORE does nothing. Counted zero hits in play.
ASCII, printed a character at a time through print_char until a byte with bit 7 set ($FF here): "Enter time of day (HH:MM am/pm)> "
The main loop. Counts passes in $09DB and writes a step number, 1 to 9, to $0930 before each stage.
CIA1 interrupt, reached through driver_jumps+$18 from the IRQ handler when the source is not the raster: timer A goes to $3F3B, timer B to $3FBF, each with interrupts re-enabled.
Split address table: eight routines, low bytes then high bytes. sound_dispatch calls one for each bit set in $478D.

The font for all on-screen text: 96 glyphs of 8 bytes, ASCII $20-$7F in order. print_char's glyph fetch ($BB29) takes (char - $20) * 8 from here; the base is the first entry of the table at $BDC0/$BDC2.
Letter text, ASCII, $0D for a new line, $FF at the end: "Dear Friend,", return, two spaces
Letter text, ASCII, $0D for a new line, $FF at the end: "Thank You," and "Your Friend", each indented eight spaces
Letter text, ASCII, $0D for a new line, $FF at the end: "Thank you for keeping me well stocked with food and water."
Letter text, ASCII, $0D for a new line, $FF at the end: "Please notice that my supplies are running low.  I can't stay happy and healthy without your support."

Jump table, three bytes an entry. $8000, $8003, $8006, $8009, $8015 and $801B are RTS stubs, and nothing in the image calls them; $800C, $800F, $8012 and $8018 jump to the timer and sound code at $394E-$39B2.

Parser word list 1 (verbs, question words, feelings and manners): each record is five bytes of concept bits, the word in upper-case ASCII, and $00. Words with the same bits are synonyms (LIKE and ENJOY; LIGHT, START, MAKE, BURN and IGNITE). $FF ends the list.
Parser word list 2 (things, rooms and games), in the same format as list 1: five bytes of concept bits, the word, $00. It ends with a record whose word is empty.

The parser's rules: 16-byte records of five bytes of list-1 concept bits, five of list-2 concept bits, then a short list of action codes ended by a byte of $80 or more. 34 rules; $FF ends the table at $CB8A.
